title: Post-quantum chat
subtitle: Two identities, generated in your browser, exchanging real post-quantum encrypted messages over public Nostr relays.
liveNotice: These are real events published to public relays. They are encrypted and use throwaway keys, but they are not simulated.

trace.identitiesDetail: Each has a 24-word seed phrase generated in your browser. The secp256k1 key and the ML-KEM and ML-DSA keys are all derived from that one seed, as siblings — no key is derived from another. Nothing has left your browser yet.

extension.title: Use your own identity
extension.notFound: No Nostr extension detected. Install the Nostr WoT extension to send from your own identity.
extension.canReceive: Your post-quantum keys are published, so Alice and Bob can message you back.
extension.cannotReceive: You can send, but not receive yet: no post-quantum attestation was found for your identity. Publish one from the extension — Menu → Security → Post-quantum key — so senders can find your ML-KEM key.
extension.sentDetail: The payload was encrypted and the seal signed by your extension. Only the outer wrap was built here, because it is signed by a throwaway key.
extension.connectHint: Connect your Nostr extension to join the conversation with your own identity.
extension.foundKey: Found your ML-KEM key in your attestation
extension.foundKeyDetail: Read off the relays, exactly as for the demo identities. Alice and Bob can now encrypt to you.
extension.noAttestation: No usable attestation for your identity
extension.noAttestationDetail: You can still send, because sending only needs the recipient's key. Nobody can send to you until you publish one from the extension.

status.publishing: Publishing each identity's attestation, so the others can find its ML-KEM key…
status.resolving: Reading the keys back off the relays — nothing is sent until they are found there.
status.failed: The attestations could not be found on any relay, so there is nothing to encrypt to. The page stops here rather than falling back to classic encryption.
status.startExplainer: Nothing has been published yet. Starting publishes one kind:10203 attestation for each identity to the relays below — that is the only way anyone learns their ML-KEM key, and the only way to send without the page cheating by reading keys out of its own memory.

faq.title: Questions about this demo
faq.subtitle: What it proves, what it does not, and what it leaves on your machine.

real.a: Yes. Every message is a real NIP-59 gift wrap published to public relays, encrypted with real ML-KEM-1024. Nothing is simulated: a message only appears once a relay hands it back and it decrypts, and each one names the relay that served it.

keys.q: Where do the post-quantum keys come from?
keys.a: From the same 24-word seed as the Nostr key, expanded a second time with HKDF under a different label. The keys are siblings, not parent and child — so recovering the Nostr private key tells an attacker nothing about the post-quantum ones.

size.q: Why is a post-quantum message so much bigger?
size.a: The ML-KEM-1024 ciphertext is 1,568 bytes, on every message, and it dominates everything else. Open any message in the event explorer and the byte map shows exactly where the size goes.

protects.a: The confidentiality of messages sent from now on, permanently — including against someone archiving them today to decrypt later. It does not stop an attacker with a quantum computer from signing events as you, because events are still signed with secp256k1.

relays.a: No. The outer gift wrap is an ordinary kind:1059 event, so post-quantum messages cross today’s relay network unmodified and clients that know nothing about this are unaffected.

stored.q: What is stored on my machine?
stored.a: Two mnemonics and the event history, in this browser’s local storage. They are disposable demo keys, kept only so a return visit reuses them instead of publishing another pair of attestations to public relays. "Generate new identities", in the event explorer, discards them.
